title: Shifted Windows (Swin)
tagline: Window attention is linear, not quadratic — and shifting alternate layers stitches the seams
summary: Global self-attention costs N^4 in the number of image patches, which does not survive high resolution. Swin restricts attention to small M-by-M windows (cost N^2 M^2, linear in tokens) and, on alternate layers, shifts the window grid by half a window so information can cross the seams. Click a patch to see exactly which others it can attend to, flip the shift toggle to watch that neighbourhood jump across a boundary, and drag the sliders to feel the N^4 versus N^2 M^2 cost gap open up.
highlights: Click any patch to light up its attention window — the exact set of patches it can talk to.
Flip the shift toggle and watch a patch near a seam land in a new window with new neighbours.
See why window attention is O(N^2 M^2), linear in tokens, while full attention is O(N^4).
Drag the grid- and window-size sliders and watch the full-attention pair count explode next to the windowed count.
Understand how alternating shifted and unshifted layers grow the receptive field across the whole image without a global attention matrix.
